subject: Show auto-detected PuTTY path on Advanced options page
body:
Show auto-detected PuTTY path on Advanced options page

Adds a read-only "Detected PuTTY:" field above the custom-path
checkbox, displaying what PuttyLocator found on the system (or a
not-detected message), so the user can confirm what mRemoteNG will
actually launch independent of the custom-path override. Updated on
page load and whenever the custom-path setting changes.

All controls below the custom-path checkbox shift down 28px to make
room for the new field.

triage.rationale: Small UX win: shows auto-detected PuTTY path in options. Our Designer/options pages diverged heavily; re-do by hand, not cherry-pick.

votes.concern: It falsely labels the fork's fixed bundled PuTTYNG.exe path as auto-detected; its source design depends on absent PuttyLocator state.
votes.reason: The fork already exposes the custom override and otherwise always launches bundled PuTTYNG.exe, so this UI is redundant, misleading, and upstream-specific.

votes.concern: Relies on unbundled PuTTY and auto-detection logic (`PuttyLocator`) that our fork does not have, since we still bundle `PuTTYNG.exe` directly.
votes.reason: Our fork bundles `PuTTYNG.exe` and has not imported the unbundling candidate. This change is redundant and will break the build due to missing auto-detection dependencies.

dissent: codex: REJECT - The fork already exposes the custom override and otherwise always launches bundled PuTTYNG.exe, so this UI is redundant, misleading, and upstream-specific.
gemini: REJECT - Our fork bundles `PuTTYNG.exe` and has not imported the unbundling candidate. This change is redundant and will break the build due to missing auto-detection dependencies.
